name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,111

clue.text: Captains bringing herring aboard ship

indicators.note: the ship brings the fish on board, so one word sits inside the other, with aboard completing the picture

blocks.note: SS is the standard abbreviation for steamship
a kipper is a split, smoked herring

explanation.surface: Ships' masters hauling a catch of herring onto the deck.
explanation.walkthrough: SKIPPERS is KIPPER inside SS. A kipper is a smoked herring, a British breakfast staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Skipper is the informal title for the master of a boat or the leader of a team.

clue.text: Aware of guru boundlessly moving from place to place

indicators.note: without its bounds, the word loses its first and last letters and keeps only its inside

blocks.note: to be onto something is to be aware of it
the inner letters of guru

explanation.surface: Someone who follows a guru who never stays in one ashram.
explanation.definitionFit: A band or troupe on tour travels between venues, performing in a series of different towns.

clue.text: Really overturned your electric car

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturning something flips it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: YR is a common abbreviation for your
EV stands for electric vehicle

explanation.surface: A news item about somebody's electric car being flipped in a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are intensifying adverbs meaning truly or extremely, as in very good or really good.

clue.text: Regularly viewed customs of saint as extreme

indicators.note: looking at a word only at regular intervals means reading every second letter of it

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of customs
o' is a shortened form of of, as in will-o'-the-wisp
St is the standard abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A traveller studying the strange customs surrounding a saint's feast and finding them extreme.
explanation.definitionFit: Utmost describes the greatest or furthest degree possible, the farthest limit of something.

clue.text: Rum do — ally is unfaithful

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange in British slang, so the letters come out in a strange order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that a strange business is afoot because a friend has turned traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum is old British slang for odd, and a do is a party or event.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone disloyal betrays trust or breaks faith, just as an unfaithful partner or friend does.

clue.text: Climber finishes in trek, he had reached highest point

indicators.note: the finishes of the following words are their final letters

blocks.note: the pea is a climbing plant
the closing letters of trek, he and had

explanation.surface: A mountaineer at the end of a long trek, having reached the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' paints a mountaineer, but here it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaked is the past tense of the verb meaning to reach a maximum or top level.

clue.text: Gun bags on the counter

indicators.note: counter means against or opposite, so the word runs in the contrary direction

blocks.note: to net something is to bag or capture it

explanation.surface: A firearm and some shopping bags lying on a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' suggests a shop counter, but it means contrary, the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sten was a cheap British submachine gun of the Second World War.

clue.text: Most gracious type is French

blocks.note: a kind is a type or sort
est is the French word for is

explanation.surface: A claim that the French are the most courteous sort of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindest is the superlative of kind, describing the most generous, considerate and gentle behaviour.

clue.text: Not moving from Bury? Time to shift position

indicators.note: shifting position means a letter is lifted out of its place before being set down elsewhere

blocks.note: to inter is to bury a body
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone who refuses to leave the town of Bury in England, though it is time to relocate.
explanation.walkthrough: The T in INTER moves from the middle to the end, giving INERT. Bury is a town near Manchester, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert describes something motionless, lacking the power or will to move or act.

clue.text: Mock husband bitten by small horse

indicators.note: something bitten is held between the jaws, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a pony is a small breed of horse
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A man nipped by a pony and laughed at for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mock as an adjective means fake or imitation, like a phony or sham version.

clue.text: Waterproof cloth ordered in kilos

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters are put into a fresh sequence

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fabric for rain gear bought by weight from a supplier.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilskin is cotton treated with oil to repel rain, used for sailors' coats and hats.

clue.text: Seriously advanced fencing around home

indicators.note: fencing something in surrounds it, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: early means advanced in time, ahead of schedule
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: A homeowner who got far ahead with putting a fence round the property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fencing' suggests the sport or a garden fence, but it signals enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something earnestly is to do it with sincere, intense conviction rather than in jest.

clue.text: Sending message to this writer laid up in poor health

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom upward

blocks.note: this writer is the setter referring to themselves
ailing means sick or unwell

explanation.surface: The setter, bedridden with illness, keeps in touch by email.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid up' reads as bedridden, which matches 'in poor health', but 'up' is doing the reversing.
explanation.definitionFit: Emailing is the act of sending an electronic message to someone.

clue.text: Heard Welshman break down

indicators.note: heard tells us we want the sound of a word rather than its spelling

blocks.note: Dai is a very common Welsh man's name, short for David

explanation.surface: A man from Wales was overheard collapsing in tears.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine or machine that dies stops working, the same as one that breaks down.

clue.text: Curse amount to hire senior employee?

blocks.note: an exec is an executive
a rate is the price charged for hiring someone or something

explanation.surface: Someone swearing at the cost of hiring a top manager.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or call down evil upon someone, a formal word for cursing them.

clue.text: Polite form of address digital assistant shortened

indicators.note: a shortened word has been cut down, losing its last letter here

blocks.note: Siri is Apple's voice assistant

explanation.surface: Telling a voice assistant to use a courteous, brief way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir is the respectful title used when speaking to a man, especially one of rank.

clue.text: Vegetable is hard to cook

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that a certain vegetable is difficult to prepare.
explanation.definitionFit: The radish is a crisp, peppery root eaten raw in salads, a kind of vegetable.

clue.text: Free a labrador locked up by a vile rogue

indicators.note: something locked up is shut inside, so one group of letters goes within the other
rogue means wayward and uncontrolled, so the combined letters run wild into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
a, plus lab, the short name for a labrador retriever

explanation.surface: A dog held captive by a wicked villain needs to be set loose.
explanation.walkthrough: A LAB goes inside A VILE, and the whole nine letters are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone free at a given time is available, with no other commitments to prevent them.

clue.text: On foreign soil, retired group in Granada or Barcelona

indicators.note: a group of letters sitting in the following words is taken out as one run
retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the run is read backwards

blocks.note: the run spans the end of Granada, the word or and the start of Barcelona

explanation.surface: A band of retirees living in a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: Granada and Barcelona set the Spanish scene, which is exactly where the answer puts us.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abroad is to be in a foreign country, away from home soil.

clue.text: Winged beast — poultry, we’re told is dirty

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so the sounds matter, not the spelling

blocks.note: a bee is a winged insect
fowl are domestic birds such as chickens

explanation.surface: Gossip that some winged creature or farmyard bird is filthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To befoul is to make something unclean or polluted, the verb dirty in a stronger form.

clue.text: Cheat musician

blocks.note: first meaning: a swindler who fiddles the books
second meaning: a violin player

explanation.walkthrough: Read together, the clue suggests a musician who cheats; they are two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddler is both a violinist and, informally, someone who swindles or falsifies accounts.

clue.text: Company not yielding to pressure

blocks.note: first meaning: a business
second meaning: solid and unbending

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a business that resists demands; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm is a noun for a commercial business and an adjective for something solid or resolute.

clue.text: Proposal cancelled, then back on

indicators.note: back tells us the word that follows is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: an event that is off has been cancelled
re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A marriage proposal called off and then reinstated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back on' reads as reinstated, but it splits: 'back' is the reversal signal and 'on' means concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: An offer is something put forward for acceptance, which is what a proposal is.

clue.text: Pained expression after losing tip of finger

indicators.note: losing the tip means the first letter of the next word is cut off

blocks.note: to finger something is to touch it

explanation.surface: Someone who has just cut off a fingertip, with the expected reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finger' reads as a noun, but it is the verb meaning to handle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouch is the exclamation people blurt out in sudden pain, so it is literally an expression of being hurt.

clue.text: Stood up ones I regret in retrospect, partially

indicators.note: partially means only part of the following words is used, as one run of letters
looking in retrospect means looking back, so the run is read backwards

blocks.note: the run spans the end of ones, the word I and the start of regret

explanation.surface: Someone recalling the dates who jilted them and whom they now regret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stood up' tempts as being jilted, matching the surface; here it means got to one's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Risen is the past participle of rise, meaning got up or stood, as in having risen from a chair.

clue.text: Caught in flying toucan’s bill

indicators.note: flying suggests letters scattered through the air and landing in a new order
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A toucan in flight seized by its enormous beak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like the toucan's beak, but it is the definition: an invoice.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is a statement of money owed, which is what a bill is.
